LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 on PyPI were compromised with a credential-stealing package; user said 'I only use it as lightweight wrapper and will most likely move away from it entirely. Not worth the risk.'
The GitHub account of LiteLLM's Founder/CTO (krrishdholakia) appears to have been fully compromised, with public repos vandalized to say 'teampcp owns BerriAI.'
'Does anyone know a good alternate project... LiteLLM has been getting worse and trying to get me to upgrade to a paid version. I also had issues with creating tokens for other users etc.'
'Now I feel lucky that I switched to just using OpenRouter a year ago because LiteLLM was incredible flaky and kept causing outages.'
'LiteLLM is the second worst software project known to man. (First is LangChain. Third is OpenClaw.)'
A user described running LiteLLM as a proxy in their homelab via the litellm/litellm docker image for local LLM gateway management, noting they were on an unaffected older version (1.77).
'That's a bad supply-chain attack, many folks use litellm as main gateway' — reflecting how widely used LiteLLM is as an LLM gateway.
PyPI quarantined the compromised LiteLLM package quickly after the report; commenters noted 'It's been quarantined on PyPI' and praised the fast turnaround.
Someone quoted LiteLLM's security certifications page (SOC 2 Type I/II, ISO 27001) sarcastically ('ROFL') in light of the compromise, mocking the value of such certifications given the breach.
Mercor reported being hit by a cyberattack tied to the LiteLLM compromise; the incident reportedly prompted LiteLLM to switch its compliance certification vendor from Delve to Vanta.

Description of the infection chain from a security researcher's investigation: 'Cursor → futuresearch-mcp-legacy (v0.6.0) → litellm (v1.82.8) → litellm_init.pth' shipped as an official PyPI wheel with the malicious file listed in the package manifest.

Show HN launch of LiteLLM Proxy Server: praised as 'super compelling' with maintainers noting motivation was avoiding messy 100-line if/else statements for reliable model switching across 50+ LLM providers.
LiteLLM maintainer confirmed proxy supports streaming and function-calling in the same way as the openai-python SDK, and added Ollama integration within hours of user requests for local LLM support.

Show HN launch of the original LiteLLM library; a user praised it: 'This is amazing. Really needed something like this to standardize all my different AI APIs! ... I love how quickly your team is shipping!'
Maintainer distinguished LiteLLM from a similar library (llm-client-sdk) by stating 'while your library looks really powerful my goal with Litellm is simplicity.'
